newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S. [CORRECTED 01:50 GMT 26/2]
newsitem.headline: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S. [CORRECTED 01:50 GMT 26/2]

text.p: Canada softwood lumber exports to the United States as of 0001 EST on February 25 in board feet, according to data from the Canadian Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade:
For the Jan 1 - March 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 7.23 mln 8.20 mln 7.17 mln 34.17 mln 56.78 mln
LFB 42.77 mln 2.46 mln 20.97 mln 35.94 mln 102.14 mln
UFB 7.39 mln 5.54 mln 17.11 mln 49.20 mln 79.23 mln
Pct exported: EB - 10.22, LFB - 15.71
For the Oct 1 - Dec 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 6.36 mln 7.66 mln 9.25 mln 51.04 mln 74.31 mln
LFB 3.81 mln 10.39 mln 6.42 mln 11.43 mln 32.05 mln
UFB 6.74 mln 12.30 mln 4.44 mln 27.38 mln 50.86 mln
Pct exported: EB - 25.18, LFB - 4.93
April 1 - present:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 13.60 mln 15.86 mln 16.42 mln 85.21 mln 131.09 mln
EB 7.68 bln 1.06 bln 1.52 bln 3.28 bln 13.54 bln
LFB 89.66 mln 17.54 mln 54.49 mln 120.88 mln 282.56 mln
UFB 14.13 mln 17.84 mln 21.55 mln 76.58 mln 130.09 mln
Pct exported: EB - 92.12 (Corrects from 91.52), LFB - 43.47 (corrects from 41.60).
Source: Export and Import Controls Bureau, Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.
NOTE: EB = established base shipments, LFB = lower fee base, UFB = upper base fee.

From April 1, Canadian lumber exports which exceed quarterly or annual quotas are subject to export fees. Exports above 14.7 billion board feet annually or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly are subject to US$50 fee for every 1,000 board feet. If such excess exports exceed 650 million board feet, they are subject to a US$100 fee for every 1,000 board feet.
Export quotas are allocated for each province on a company-by-company basis. Shippers who have not been given an allocation are subject to the US$100 fee for any lumber they export.
This export data is based on Canadian export permits. There is a one-week lag between the entry of softwood lumber into the United States and the application for a Canadian permit.
